ops.title: Flaky on CI: ServiceSocketClientDeadlineTests' fixed wall-clock deadline assertions
ops.description:
`Tests/DaemonKitTests/ServiceSocketClientDeadlineTests.swift` drives real unix sockets with **fixed wall-clock deadlines** and has now failed twice on hosted runners, on two different assertions, from unrelated pushes. The pattern is the assertion, not the code under test.

## Occurrences

**2026-07-29, run `30414335805`** (commit `a73e6c3`) — `writeTimeoutWithOpenDeadlineReplaysIdempotentCallOnSuccessor` at `:579` failed with `ReadinessNoProgressError` after 5.049s. The push was **Go-only**: four commits touching `wire/`, `service/`, `trust/`+`codeidentity/`, and `proc/`, with no `Sources/` or `Tests/` file changed anywhere in the range. Green on the next run.

**2026-07-24, run `30079880059`** — `brokerHandoffTerminalResponseCannotOutliveFixedDeadline` in the same file tripped a `< 0.15s` bound at 0.186s, also on an unrelated change.

## Why this is a test defect, not a product defect

A `< 0.15s` bound on a shared GitHub runner is a machine-speed constant, not an invariant — the same class of assertion the Go side has already been bitten by (`proc`'s `waitManagerChild` 3s budget, backlog `29a01af`/`243d40c`). A hosted runner's scheduling jitter dwarfs the margin, and the 2026-07-29 run showed corroborating noise (Homebrew tap-trust warnings in the same job's Format/Lint steps).

The property these tests exist to prove is **ordering and causality** — that a response cannot outlive its deadline, that a successor replays an idempotent call — not that the machine hit a particular millisecond. Re-express them against an injectable clock or a measured baseline rather than a literal, the same way the Go side's `wiretest` harness advances a clock manually instead of sleeping.

## Why it matters beyond the annoyance

daemonkit's CI is the release gate, and the standing rule is *fleet-build or mixed-era red = no release, ever*. A gate that red-lights clean pushes trains everyone to re-run without reading, which is exactly how 18,999 handshake failures stayed invisible behind green CI. Two flaky families on the Go side plus one on the Swift side is already past the point where re-running is reflex.

ops.text: ServiceSocketClientDeadlineTests asserts ordering and causality rather than fixed wall-clock magnitudes, or bounds them against a measured baseline
The suite passes 20 consecutive runs on a hosted macOS runner
Any remaining literal timing bound carries a comment naming what it measures and why that magnitude
